# Brief 23: debts held outside Wealthsimple, read from Wealthsimple's net worth feature: what exists, how it is read, what it supports

**Asked (owner, 2026-10-11):** whether Bagholder can take in debts held outside Wealthsimple through Wealthsimple's own linked-accounts feature; the best way to discover the queries; and what to show (the Cashflow tile with external interest and repayments beside margin interest; a more complete net asset value or a debt ratio on the Portfolio tab).

**Investigated:** Wealthsimple's public web bundle (release `0.3.688170`, read 2026-10-11: `https://assets.wealthsimple.com/app-24757da107ccf8c6.js` and the 85 chunks its `/app/net-worth` and `/app/connected-accounts-hub` routes load), its help centre (articles 47404070566555 "Track your individual and household net worth", updated 2026-09-22; 360056580394 "Link a bank account", 2026-10-07; 40878485117979 "What is open banking?", 2026-10-05; 29864334540699 "Create a Wealthsimple household", 2026-10-05; read through the help centre's own JSON API, since its HTML pages refuse non-browser clients), its Product Insider post "Households: your whole financial picture in one place" (2026-09-08), Plaid's and Flinks' documentation, the documentation of nine portfolio trackers and seven trading journals, and the definitions of net worth, the debt-to-asset ratio and the treatment of interest and principal in a cash-flow statement. Every claim below was re-fetched and checked against its page by a second reader; the full list with quotes is in `23/research.json`.

## 1. What Wealthsimple exposes

**The feature.** "Net worth" (web: "Select the Net worth tab from the left side menu"; app: Home → Net worth). It covers "All Wealthsimple account you hold, Any external accounts you've linked through this feature, Any external accounts you added manually through this feature". Linking "allows you to automatically pull balances for investments and bank accounts into your net worth view"; what cannot be linked, "such as real estate, vehicles, or specific loans", is added by hand as "an Asset or a Liability (such as a mortgage or loan)" with "the account name, type, and current value", and updated by hand ("Update balance, insert the new value and date"). Wealthsimple's own description: "Net worth on Wealthsimple shows everything you own and owe — not just the Wealthsimple parts. You can link external accounts like a mortgage or an investment account at another institution, and manually add cash, assets, and debts like a home, a car, or a credit card balance." (Product Insider, 2026-09-08.)

**Freshness.** "Since open banking isn't yet supported in Canada, external account balances may not update automatically. You can update them manually… Log in with your institution credentials if prompted." And: "each financial institution provides a different (and often incomplete) set of information about an account. Some provide investment holdings data, others have transactions, and some provide mortgage details." So a linked balance is as current as the person's last refresh at Wealthsimple, and a manual one as current as their last entry; each carries its own as-of moment (below).

**Aggregators.** For bank linking Wealthsimple names "Flinks, Plaid, or our in-house Wealthsimple Connection Tool (WST)" and says "Linking an account to deposit funds isn't the same as linking an account to track net worth." The bundle's net-worth code carries `AggregatorConnectionMetadata` as `FlinksConnectionMetadata | WstConnectionMetadata` and a `PlaidLinkTokenCreate` mutation. Which one serves which institution is not published.

**The API.** Same endpoint and session the app already holds (`my.wealthsimple.com/graphql`, `wealthsimple/src/client.rs:17`). The documents, rebuilt from the bundle, are in `23/graphql/`:

- `FetchIdentityNetWorthAccounts($identityId, $filter)` → `identity.netWorth.accounts` (Wealthsimple's own, each with `financials.currentCombined.netLiquidationValueV2` and `creditCard.current`) and `externalFinancialEntities`, each: `id: canonicalId`, `entityType`, `displayName: name`, `institutionName`, `currency`, `balance: currentBalance {amount currency}`, `balanceAsOf: currentBalanceAsOf`, `updatedAt`, `aggregatorLink {id aggregator error {type}}` (absent for a manual entry), `ownershipType`, `visibility {household}`; a mortgage adds `interestRate`, `monthlyPayment {amount}`, `remainingAmortizationMonths`.
- `FetchIdentityNetWorthFinancials($identityId, $accountIds, $externalFinancialEntityIds, $currency, $startDate, $endDate, $first, $accountScope)` → `netWorth.financials.current(currency) {balance}` and `historicalDaily(currency, startDate, endDate, first)`, one `{date balance}` per day, for whichever set of accounts and entities is named: the whole net worth, or the liabilities alone. The page asks `startDate`/`endDate` as `yyyy-MM-dd` for 1w/1m/3m/6m/ytd/1y and `2014-01-01` for "all"; `accountScope` is `OWN` or `HOUSEHOLD`.
- `FetchIdentityNetWorthFinancialsWithBreakdowns` → `current.breakdown(groups) {key balance}`; the page groups into `CHEQUING_AND_SAVINGS`, `INVESTMENTS`, `LIABILITIES`, `REAL_ESTATE_AND_VALUABLES`, `UNCATEGORIZED`, the grouping done in the client from each entity's `entityType`.
- Entity kinds (33, from the bundle's type map): AutoLoan, Car, Cd, Chequing, CreditCard, Crypto, Fhsa, GroupNonRegistered, GroupRrsp, GroupTfsa, Heloc, InstallmentLoan, Lif, LineOfCredit, Lira, Margin, MoneyMarket, Mortgage, NonRegistered, OtherAsset, OtherInvestment, OtherLiability, PersonalLoan, RealEstate, RespFamily, RespIndividual, Rrif, Rrsp, Savings, SpousalRrif, SpousalRrsp, StudentLoan, Tfsa.
- The page's own words: "Outstanding balance" ("You can update this anytime."), "Last updated", "Interest rate" and "Monthly payment" (mortgage), "Refresh", "{n} accounts lost connection".

**What is not there.** No operation returns a transaction, an interest charge or a payment of an external account; the only per-liability detail beyond a balance is the mortgage's stated rate, payment and amortization. Plaid's Liabilities product does carry `interest_charge_amount`, `last_payment_amount` and a mortgage's year-to-date interest and principal (plaid.com/docs/api/products/liabilities), and Flinks returns 90 or 365 days of transactions (docs.flinks.com), but Wealthsimple passes none of it to its client, and Plaid itself calls its Canadian liabilities coverage limited.

## 2. How the queries are discovered: the method, made repeatable

The repository's method is the right one (`docs/plans/stage-3b-wealthsimple.md:41`: "recovered from Wealthsimple's public web bundle… each file naming the bundle release"). It is reproducible without a sign-in and without clicking through screens, which is why it beats watching the browser's network panel (incomplete, unrepeatable, and the owner's data in every reply):

1. `GET https://my.wealthsimple.com/app/home` names the main bundle; the bundle holds `__webpack_require__.u` (chunk id → `<id>-<hash>.js` under `https://assets.wealthsimple.com/`) and, per route, the chunk ids it loads (`case r.startsWith("/app/net-worth")`).
2. The documents in the main bundle carry their source (`loc.source.body`); those in the newer chunks do not, so each `{kind:"Document"…}` is parsed and printed back to GraphQL, fragments resolved by spread. `23/ws-bundle-documents.py` (120 lines, standard library) does this and produced the files in `23/graphql/`; it found 187 operations and 235 fragments across the chunks read.
3. The shapes of the replies come from the owner's own session on a copy of the book, through the app's client, recorded and anonymised with the existing `ws-anonymise` into `wealthsimple/tests/replies` (institution names and balances are identifying; the repository is public).

**Recommended regardless of this feature:** make step 2 a `bin` of the `wealthsimple` crate and a test that every shipped `.graphql` equals the current bundle's text for that operation, so drift is found by a run, not by a failed pull. Stage 3b did that check by hand once (2026-09-24); the tool makes it a command. It is tooling, not a feature.

## 3. What the data supports

**The Cashflow idea: no source.** The Cashflow tile's margin interest is real rows (the Interest charge rows of the activity feed, `SPEC.md` cashflow-7, cashflow-11). Nothing equivalent exists for an outside debt: Wealthsimple states balances, not charges or payments. Deriving interest or repayments from the change in a balance would be a made-up figure (a balance moves by interest, payments, new borrowing and fees at once), and the mortgage's "Monthly payment" is a schedule, not a flow that happened. Nothing synthetic goes on a chart; verified sources only. Not buildable as asked; nothing in the category does it either (Empower's cash flow is income against expense; Kubera's "cash flow" is an asset's own contributions; Portfolio Performance records an interest charge only as a transaction the person types).

**The Portfolio idea: supported, as two figures Wealthsimple states.** Net asset value is the investment accounts' net liquidation value and should stay what it is. What the owner is after is net worth, a different figure: assets minus liabilities (Statistics Canada; every tracker that has liabilities: Kubera "assets minus debts", Wealthica, Empower, Ghostfolio). Wealthsimple computes it and states it (`netWorth.financials.current`). The debt-to-asset ratio is total liabilities over total assets, a solvency measure (Iowa State Extension; OpenStax); no tracker documents one, so showing it is the owner's choice, but its definition is not.

## 4. Proposal

Portfolio tab, two tiles, shown only when Wealthsimple's net-worth view holds anything beyond the person's Wealthsimple accounts (else nothing changes):

- **Net worth**: Wealthsimple's own figure for the person's scope (`OWN`), in CAD as it states it; subtitle, in the style of Net asset value's `N accounts, N positions`: the count of accounts outside Wealthsimple it includes.
- **Debt**: the liabilities' balances as Wealthsimple states them, converted to CAD, shown positive; margin excluded, since Margin used already shows it; the Wealthsimple credit card's balance included, which today the app reads (`FetchCreditCardAccount`) and shows nowhere (portfolio-7: "a debt, not margin, and not counted"); subtitle `y% of assets`, the debt-to-asset ratio over Wealthsimple's own asset total, in the style of Margin used's share.

Behind them: each external entity kept as Wealthsimple states it, the Type 2 way the statements are about to be kept (brief 22), with its own as-of moment, read on the pull's cadence (two queries per sync, never per balances read), scope a parameter. Both phones gain the same two tiles (`SPEC.md` §8, the-phone-16). The daily series Wealthsimple keeps (`historicalDaily`) is read for nothing now; a net-worth line beside the equity curve would be a feature of its own later.

What it costs: a plan through the gate, a `SPEC.md` change (the Portfolio tiles, portfolio-7's credit-card sentence, §8), a book migration, two new recorded reply shapes, and both apps. Under the owner's own rule (decisions, 2026-10-04: no new features until the bugs and slop are fixed) it waits its turn; this brief is so that nothing has to be rediscovered when it comes up. The bundle tool of §2 can go first; it is not a feature.

## For the owner

- Cashflow: not possible from Wealthsimple's data; I advise against inventing it from balance changes.
- Portfolio: Net worth and Debt tiles as above, if you want them, when the queue allows.
- Whether to build the bundle tool now, ahead of the feature.
